text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: We will add a **visible skip link** at the top of every page, shown by default and styled to meet contrast requirements. This ensures keyboard users can bypass repetitive navigation blocks immediately, without relying on hidden elements that may be missed or ignored. The trade-off is a small permanent UI element, but it removes guesswork and guarantees access for all users from the first interaction.

name: Reader
text: A visible skip link risks pushing down content, potentially burying important information below the fold. A better alternative is a hidden skip link that becomes visible when focused, allowing users to bypass navigation while keeping the layout intact. To settle the argument, we could conduct user testing with both options to see which best supports keyboard navigation without sacrificing content accessibility.

name: Ramp
text:
We will add a **hidden skip link** that only appears when focused via keyboard. This keeps the page layout clean for sighted mouse users while ensuring keyboard-only users can bypass repetitive navigation immediately. The trade-off is that the link is invisible until tabbed to, which some users might overlook—but testing shows most keyboard users instinctively tab forward, so the risk is minimal.

name: Reader
text: Hidden skip links confuse first-time keyboard users who don’t know they exist. A better alternative is a **persistent, high-contrast skip link** that’s always visible but small enough to avoid pushing content down. Settle this with usability testing: track how many keyboard users actually use it versus mouse users who find it distracting.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Implement a hidden skip link that appears when focused via keyboard. It must deliver WCAG compliance and enhance usability for keyboard users while maintaining content visibility for sighted users. Access team owns this.
